## Findings
- claim-1: For every bigrassmannian parameter tuple, the lower family \(\{\bar s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(i^j,b^a)\}\) generates \(J_v\), and no member can be removed. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 220-235]
- claim-2: The homogeneous no-syzygy theorem used to prove lower-family minimality holds integrally in \(\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\). [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 819-831]
- claim-3: The right family is the conjugate family \(\{\bar s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq((i+a)^b,i^{j-b})\}\), and its generation was proved in the transposed version. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 833-840]
- claim-4: For \(i=j=3,\ a=2,\ b=3,\ r=n-r=5\), both displayed ten-element families map to \(\mathbb Z\)-bases of \(J/A_+J\).
- claim-5: In the degreewise orders specified below, the transition from the lower basis to the right basis is \(\operatorname{diag}(1,-1,I_2,-I_2,I_2,-1,1)\), hence is unimodular.
## Strategy
Let \(L_\rho=\bar s_{(3^3,\rho)}\) and \(R_{\rho'}=\omega(L_\rho)\), for \(\rho\subseteq3^2\). Both families have degree profile \(1,1,2,2,2,1,1\) in weights \(9,\ldots,15\).

Use lower-family generation and the integral no-syzygy theorem [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 220-235; 819-831] to show the \(L_\rho\) form a \(\mathbb Z\)-basis of \(J/A_+J\): \(J\) begins in weight \(9\), so \((A_+J)_9=0\); in higher excess degree \(N\), a nonzero integral dependence modulo \(A_+J\) expands, via lower-family generation, to the forbidden homogeneous syzygy.

Since \(\omega(\bar s_\lambda)=\bar s_{\lambda'}\) preserves the self-conjugate quotient \(\Lambda/I_{5,5}\), \(J=[3^3,5^5]\), and \(A_+\), it sends the lower basis to the right basis. Thus the right family is also a \(\mathbb Z\)-basis.

## Gaps
The requested target is **not established**. The basis argument above can establish existence of a degreewise unimodular transition, but not the requested explicit transition.

In particular, the asserted congruences
\[
R_{\rho'}\equiv (-1)^{|\rho|}L_\rho\pmod{A_+J}
\]
and resulting diagonal matrix
\[
\operatorname{diag}(1,-1,I_2,-I_2,I_2,-1,1)
\]
lack explicit integral witnesses in \(A_+J\). The cited antipode identity does not by itself supply those witnesses.

## Next
For every \(\rho\subseteq3^2\), provide an exact identity
\[
R_{\rho'}-(-1)^{|\rho|}L_\rho
=\sum_k a_k h_{t_k}\bar s_{\lambda_k},
\qquad 1\le t_k\le5,\quad \bar s_{\lambda_k}\in J.
\]
Equivalently, extract quotient-coordinate witnesses from complete degree-\(9\) through degree-\(15\) Pieri matrices.
